Hi Asha — thanks for the heads up.

Attached is a first-pass runbook (runbook-draft-v1.pdf) that outlines the execution steps for a temporary cross-region routing window and the controls we will apply. High-level summary:
- Scope: only tokenized inference requests for account GLB-4721 will be eligible for transient failover. No bulk reprocessing.
- Duration cap: 96 hours by default; ops can request an extension but that requires formal approval and a DPA addendum.
- KV/prefix caching: disabled for affected route to avoid persisted keys crossing regions.
- Telemetry: aggregated metrics (no PII) are exported for service health; request-level traces are stored in-region and will be redacted in any exported diagnostics.
- Audit logs: full audit trail retained for 90 days (configurable), with immediate export to your SIEM if requested.

Marissa/Ben — please review the attached and add any operational caveats (especially around cache behavior and KMS handoffs). Asha — I have flagged two items that will need legal sign-off: a short DPA addendum for the transient window, and a confirmation on subprocessor visibility.

Attachments: runbook-draft-v1.pdf

Best,

Soojin — quick inline notes on the runbook draft (see inline bullets):

- "Scope": good start. Recommend adding an explicit allowlist by route+model version to ensure we don't accidentally include analytics endpoints.
- "KV/prefix caching": instead of fully disabling, propose we set ephemeral TTL = 0 for prefix cache writes and enforce read-only from in-region cache where feasible — this reduces cold-start cost while ensuring no new cross-border keys are persisted.
- "Telemetry": callout that aggregated metrics exported to the US will be limited to resource metrics (CPU, token QPS) and anonymized error buckets; remove request-id propagation across regions.
- "Audit logs": suggest 30-day operational retention by default and an option for 90-day upon customer request — operational teams typically prefer shorter retention during temporary windows. Also confirm whether audit logs include URL-level traces (they should not).

Ben — can you confirm the KMS flow when the failover route is activated (is there an automated KMS rewrap or do we proxy to in-region key?).

I'll mark these items on the attached PDF and send back a v1.1.

Marissa
